Nei primi minuti aggredisce alto, recupera palloni nella metà campo avversaria e costringe il Milan ad abbassare il ritmo delle proprie uscite. La traversa di Masini è il simbolo di un avvio in cui gli ospiti mettono pressione e ci provano con tutte le caratteristiche che abbiamo ammirato finora. La squadra di Amorim, però, non si lascia trascinare dalla frenesia e aspetta il momento giusto per fare male. Il doppio vantaggio nasce anche dalla qualità individuale: Rabiot è protagonista con due giocate da leader, prima favorendo l'azione che porta all'autogol di Calvani, poi partecipando alla costruzione del raddoppio firmato Gonçalo Ramos. Il francese conferma di essere molto più di un centrocampista di quantità: è diventato un riferimento tecnico e mentale.

Il Frosinone, però, non crolla e con Masini trova il gol che riapre tutto. È una fase importante perché certifica il valore della vittoria del Milan: non arriva contro una squadra doma, ma contro un avversario capace di creare problemi... fino a un certo punto.

According to recent reports, la ripresa mette in mostra il lato più impressionante della squadra di Amorim, che punisce subito. Jashari, appena entrato, firma il 3-1 con una conclusione di grande potenza e indirizza definitivamente la sfida. Da quel momento emerge la differenza principale tra le due squadre: il Milan ha giocatori capaci di "spaccare" il match, le transizioni diventano un'arma devastante, con Cissé che trova la rete del poker dopo il controllo del VAR e Pulisic che approfitta di un errore difensivo per chiudere definitivamente i conti.

È un Milan che continua a crescere e che sembra aver trovato una propria identità. Amorim chiede intensità, coraggio e partecipazione collettiva: contro il Frosinone arrivano tutte queste componenti. La classifica certifica il rendimento, con sei vittorie nelle ultime sette giornate, ma è soprattutto la gestione della partita a lasciare il segnale più importante. Questo Milan non vince soltanto quando domina: sa farlo anche quando deve aspettare, soffrire e colpire al momento giusto.

Sources indicate that “I’m playing a lot, it’s great to be playing. Playing a lot of games for Milan, and it’s even better to win games.”.

In a recent development, it’s all great, but it wasn’t a given: you’ve earned this place as leader. Do you now feel like a leader of this AC Milan?

Industry observers note that “I feel good at this Milan club, and as I always say, I try to give what I can. It’s also true that I might have a more vital position this year. That might be true, but I always try to do my part, give my all, and help my teammates.”.

Recent findings suggest that it’s clear, evident, that Amorim holds you in high regard, but what is Amorim like? An adjective.

Is it true that he got very angry after the defeat against Ferencvaros?

“Yes, but I think the whole group felt that we had played a very poor game, so, as I saw it, my teammates saw it too.”.

According to recent reports, are Ferencvaros and Bologna two games you’re ready to say “never again” to? Will Frosinone be a different team?

“Yes, exactly, as I said, we are very confident, but sometimes even too much so, and then all matches are difficult against whoever we play against, and we have to understand this quickly and we can’t make the same mistakes.”.

Among the various critics, it’s said that this AC Milan team has enormous potential, but there are too many ups and downs. Does it need more consistency?

“Yes, I think it hurts even more when we lose because we know we can do well, we can win every game. So yes, when we really lose, in the locker room you feel like we’ve let ourselves down first and then everyone else.”.

Recent findings suggest that you recently became the father of a beautiful baby girl. What are your nights like as a dad?

“At night, I’m fine. My girlfriend is working really hard, so it’s a lot for me. I mean, I get up sometimes, but it’s much quieter. I think it’s harder for her.”.

And how much has life changed with the arrival of a daughter?

You were also used as a full-back, but now you only play as a centre-back….

But yes, it’s true that I’ve played a few games there in the past, but I’m happy playing as a centre back and I’m happy that the coach sees that too.”.

“I mean, crazy in a good way, yes. He likes to have fun, he likes to dance, he likes to talk, so he’s a bright spot, as they say, for the locker room, yes.”.

According to recent reports, “Well, that’s a good question. Yes, I miss her. I thought about it even when the little girl was born: I also want to score a goal, I mean, dedicate a goal to her, so I miss her, yes.”.

According to recent reports, how do you concentrate when you’re in the hotel retreat? How do you focus in the hours leading up to kick-off?

In a recent development, “It’s become a routine now, so I always do the same things. You’re in the hotel, you take a shower, you play a little video game or you’re on your phone, so now I don’t even think about it, it’s really become a routine.”.

What does Maignan ask of you, defenders?

“He indicates to stay focused on the game because, as we know, one moment can change the game and at Milan it can also change a season, so it’s very important not to underestimate every moment and always stay focused.

It seems to me that there is a great understanding between you and Strahinja Pavlovic even off the pitch….

According to recent reports, “Yes, it’s true, he and I have a good relationship; we met last year. Then when you see him you might not think, I mean, I didn’t think he would be such a great friend, but we got along really well both on and off the pitch, it’s really nice to spend time with him.”.

According to recent reports, “This is difficult, but he started at a much higher level than me. But now I’ve improved a lot, although I have to say he’s even stronger. But yes, every day we start with a game of ping pong and then we start working.”.

Industry observers note that would you like your daughter to play soccer in the future? Are you planning a second child? Would you like to have a son who plays soccer?

  • In a recent development, una partita destinata a restare impressa nella memoria di questa Serie A.
  • Recent findings suggest that nel post-partita, ai microfoni di DAZN, Cristian Chivu ha espresso tutta la propria amarezza per una vittoria sfumata nel finale: “C'è grande rammarico, si pensava di gestire un po' le cose poi abbiamo fallito la prova di maturità nei minuti finali per leggerezza.
  • Di umore differente Maurizio Sarri, soddisfatto della reazione dei suoi ma ancora preoccupato per le difficoltà difensive.

In a recent development, una partita destinata a restare impressa nella memoria di questa Serie A. Atalanta e Inter pareggiano 4-4 alla New Balance Arena, al termine di novanta minuti caratterizzati da gol, rimonte e continui colpi di scena. La squadra di Cristian Chivu conduce praticamente per tutta la gara grazie a uno straordinario Pio Esposito, autore di una tripletta, ma viene raggiunta nel recupero dal rigore di Franck Kessié. Dopo aver mantenuto la porta inviolata contro Feyenoord e Como, l'Inter subisce quattro reti in una sola serata e spreca una grande occasione nella corsa al vertice. I nerazzurri salgono a 29 punti, ma scivolano al terzo posto, a tre lunghezze dalla Lazio capolista, dopo il successo della Roma. L'Atalanta, invece, resta dodicesima a quota 15, ritrovando però carattere e fiducia dopo settimane complicate.

Recent findings suggest that nel post-partita, ai microfoni di DAZN, Cristian Chivu ha espresso tutta la propria amarezza per una vittoria sfumata nel finale: “C'è grande rammarico, si pensava di gestire un po' le cose poi abbiamo fallito la prova di maturità nei minuti finali per leggerezza. È difficile da spiegare, facciamo i complimenti all'Atalanta. Abbiamo usato un po' di leggerezza e superficialità, siamo stati un po' più leggeri del solito. Sono due punti regalati”. Il tecnico ha individuato soprattutto nell'atteggiamento il problema della sua squadra: “Dobbiamo lavorare sull'atteggiamento, sulla grinta e determinazione”. Poi un ulteriore richiamo: “I gol concessi sono troppi, non vado a guardare indietro ma dobbiamo imparare tutti che bisogna mettercela tutta in campo. Non bisogna pensare a gestire, dare il massimo fino a che l'arbitro non fischia la fine”.

Di umore differente Maurizio Sarri, soddisfatto della reazione dei suoi ma ancora preoccupato per le difficoltà difensive. L'allenatore dell'Atalanta ha spiegato a DAZN: “La squadra ha dei pregi a livello caratteriale, nelle ultime partite siamo pericolosi davanti ma ci portiamo dietro il difetto della fragilità difensiva. Troppi errori, la sensazione è quella di una squadra in crescita”. Sarri ha poi individuato negli infortuni e nella mancanza di continuità della linea arretrata alcune delle cause dei problemi. Infine, parole importanti per Charles De Ketelaere, autore di una doppietta decisiva nella rimonta: “Sta facendo bene da un mese ed è un giocatore forte fisicamente e tecnicamente. Ha potenzialità straordinarie, deve risolvere gli alti e bassi perché ha un potenziale che ho visto in pochi”. Un pareggio che non risolve tutti i problemi della Dea, ma può rappresentare una svolta dal punto di vista del morale.

£1.2m Blackburn Rovers man has a chance to lock down a starting spot, beginning with crucial Burnley tie: Opinion

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday.
  • Industry observers note that damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu.
  • In a recent development, summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday. It’s a big occasion at Ewood Park, not only because of the rivalry, but because it marks Rovers’ first game since Tony Mowbray stepped back as head coach due to health issues earlier this week.

Industry observers note that damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu. The Nigerian international has undergone surgery on his knee and is set to be sidelined until the Newly introduced Year.

In a recent development, summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City. And, he played the full 90 minutes against West Ham while the medical staff waited for a verdict on Alebiosu’s blow.

Now that we know how long Blackburn Rovers’ go-to right-back will be out for, Beyuku has a real chance to make the starting role his own.

Most clubs have at least two players to cover in every position, and that is the case at Blackburn Rovers. With Alebiosu out, Beyuku is the only natural senior right-back available for selection, paving the way for him to come into the side.

Sources indicate that A reported fee of around £1.2m was paid to sign the 20-year-old from Modena in the summer, so there is clear belief in his potential. It was widely expected that Beyuku would be cover and competition for Alebiosu, but the injury thrusts him into the limelight.

Sources indicate that he’s shown signs of growing into Championship football early on as well. His second-half against West Ham was the best we’ve seen from Beyuku to date, offering a lively presence up and down the right-hand side.

It has been revealed that the Frenchman saw to his duties at the back with 10 defensive contributions, but he was forward-thinking and frequently involved in possession like Alebiosu as well. Beyuku completed 26 of his 29 passes, nine of which were line-breaking.

He was dispossessed twice, but this does come with the territory of being a progressive right-back who is still developing and settling into a new league (all stats via FotMob).

Industry observers note that alebiosu’s shoes are big ones to fill. It might not have been planned that Beyuku would assume a starting role this early into his Blackburn Rovers, given his age and need to grow into Championship football.

It means that, despite the fact he needs to deliver, there should be an element of patience.

Recent findings suggest that if Johnson and Dodds feel Beyuku needs to be taken out of the side, there are options to consider. Kristi Montgomery has a key role in midfield alongside Sam Morsy but he has covered at right-back before. Matty Litherland is working his way back from injury too, while Lewis Miller is a longer-term absentee.

In a recent development, beyuku will have the firm backing of the Rovers faithful. A strong display against arch-rivals Burnley this Sunday would be a sure-fire way for the youngster to endear himself to the fans and announce himself in Championship football.

Gabriele Borsa is a name that AC Milan will hope to hear more of in the coming years, and those years have now been secured.

Earlier this year, Gerry Cardinale admitted that he wanted to prioritise pathways from the academy to the first team, even with prepares to invest more. Indeed, after the failure to re-sign Mattia Liberali, he’s been focused on ensuring they remain in control of the stars of tomorrow.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that so, the news of a renewal for Alphadjo Cisse is not a shock, nor is it shocking that Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto were given first-team deals in the summer. Whilst Borsa isn’t there yet, he hopefully will be one day.

Milan have done fantastically with Borsa, though. As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the 16-year-old has already signed his first professional deal with the club – posing in front of the Futuro logo – and this may seem like just another renewal.

However, he’s an investment for the future. The Rossoneri believe he’s one of the best prospects in the academy and they want to take a chance on him and they weren’t the only ones. In fact, Manchester City had been sniffing around, but they’ve been pushed back by this renewal.

A ‘modest striker who lives for goals‘, Borsa is certainly one for the future and the jump to the Futuro will hopefully be another easy step for him. Importantly, he’s not another Francesco Camarda and he will be given the time to find his feet.

With consistent goals – which come in all manners already – he’ll learn with the Futuro and probably struggle occasionally. With Sergio Navarro’s guidance, though, he could become special.
